title: Demonstrate a plausible chemical transition from nonlife to evolution

concept.text: Demonstrate an experimentally connected chemical route from plausibly available nonliving starting materials to a population that reproduces with heritable variation and adapts over successive generations. The essential advance would be showing how the stages work together: producing information-bearing molecules, copying them, maintaining variation and allowing selection to change the population. A collection of successful but chemically disconnected reactions would not establish this transition.

Scope synthesis: The endpoint is the emergence of an evolving chemical system, without requiring the construction of a modern cell. A plausible route could involve changing environmental conditions, but its sequence of inputs, transfers and transformations would need an explicit chemical and geochemical justification. Supplying a replication catalyst at the outset can demonstrate an important intermediate capability; demonstrating its emergence within the route would address a different and more demanding question.

significance.text: A successful demonstration would establish one possible chemical transition into biological evolution under specified conditions. Origin-of-life hypotheses are already experimentally testable; the revolutionary advance would be connecting their component processes through an adaptive endpoint and making that complete route available for direct experimental investigation. The supplied RNA replication work illustrates the value of resolving a specific compatibility obstacle, while leaving the larger transition unestablished.

Scientific-impact synthesis: Such a system would let researchers investigate when heredity becomes reliable enough for adaptation, which environmental changes support or disrupt that transition, and how chemical organization becomes subject to sustained selection. Conditional downstream possibilities include comparing alternative origin routes and developing new evolving chemical systems. These possibilities depend on the system's controllability and generality; one successful route would not establish that life's emergence is easy, common or inevitable.

Historical-scope synthesis: Demonstrating a possible route would not identify the route actually taken on early Earth. That historical claim would require independent geological and chemical evidence connecting the laboratory conditions and sequence of events to ancient environments. Nor would an evolving molecular population automatically possess the metabolism, compartmentalization or organizational complexity of a modern cell.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central missing capability is chemical continuity across the transition. Products of one stage must become usable inputs to the next under conditions that preserve essential molecules and functions. Attwater and colleagues provide a concrete example of the difficulty: conditions favoring RNA strand separation oppose those favoring RNA synthesis. Their experiments reconcile this particular conflict through controlled pH and freeze–thaw cycling, demonstrating why compatibility must be tested rather than assumed.

The replication work also exposes the gap between operating a chemical copying system and explaining its origin. The experiments use an existing, artificially evolved polymerase ribozyme and supplied activated RNA substrates, with controlled reagent additions and replenishment. A connected origin route would have to account for the availability or formation of the necessary substrates and functional machinery, and explain how these remain compatible with repeated copying. The reported replication experiments do not supply that complete account.

Scientific and engineering synthesis: The adaptive endpoint adds another barrier. Copying must preserve enough information for beneficial changes to persist while allowing variation on which selection can act. Researchers must distinguish heritable improvement from temporary chemical enrichment, sequence drift or repeated external provision of an advantageous component. Environmental cycling may legitimately drive the chemistry, but the route must explain why its cycles, concentrations, transfers and replenishment are plausible and which functions depend on operator intervention.

current_state.text: Attwater et al., in “Trinucleotide substrates under pH–freeze–thaw cycles enable open-ended exponential RNA replication by a polymerase ribozyme,” published May 28, 2025, DOI 10.1038/s41557-025-01830-y, report exponential RNA replication under controlled cycles. The system uses an existing artificial heterodimeric polymerase ribozyme evolved in vitro, supplied with triphosphorylated trinucleotide substrates. Its results establish a relevant RNA copying capability under specified laboratory conditions.

The paper reports fragmentary self-replication and the emergence of sequence pools during cycling, including replication and selection of replicable RNAs from libraries. These findings require careful interpretation. Fragmentary self-replication does not establish autonomous reproduction of the entire catalytic system, and emergence of RNA products without supplied sequence seeds does not mean that the replication machinery originated from simple feedstocks. The reported exponential phase was finite and followed by plateauing; the title's use of “open-ended” does not establish unlimited exponential growth.

The demonstrated advance is the integration of strand separation and copying through pH and freeze–thaw cycles. It does not establish a continuous route from simple prebiotic starting materials to an evolving system that produces its own replication machinery. Copying, changing sequence pools and fragmentary self-replication are relevant intermediate achievements, but they do not by themselves demonstrate sustained heritable adaptation following the proposed origin sequence.

Evidence scope: The supplied review assessed the complete article text, including its explicit results and methods descriptions. Figure images, linked supplementary methods and raw data were not supplied or inspected in that review, so the account here describes the reported results without claiming independent validation of those underlying materials. The supplied record contains no subsequent literature search establishing whether the complete transition had been achieved, or remained unachieved, as of November 1, 2026. That coverage gap leaves the later field-wide status unresolved.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: Document a connected sequence beginning with geochemically plausible inputs and conditions and ending with a replicating population that shows sustained, observable adaptation to a changed environment. Track material transfers and chemical transformations between stages, and demonstrate that their conditions are compatible. A modern cell is not required. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established standards endorsed by the supplied paper.
completion_criteria.label: Connected geochemically plausible route yields replicating population with sustained adaptation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed adaptation test: Specify the environmental challenge, observation period and number of generations or replication cycles before evaluating the outcome. Show that descendants retain a performance advantage under controlled comparison and connect that advantage to inherited variation. Appropriate controls should distinguish adaptation from transient enrichment, chemical drift and externally imposed replacement of the population. No numerical duration or performance threshold is established by the supplied evidence.
completion_criteria.label: Descendants retain performance advantages linked to inherited variation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed provenance and intervention requirements: Identify the origin and preparation of every supplied catalyst, activated substrate and other functional component. Disclose reagent additions, purification, transfers, replenishment and environmental cycling, and explain their possible natural counterparts. If a crucial replication component must be supplied in a form that the route cannot generate or plausibly obtain, describe the result as a demonstrated intermediate rather than completion of the full transition.
completion_criteria.label: Report all functional component origins and external interventions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and boundary tests: Repeat the complete sequence across independent runs and seek reproduction by an independent laboratory. Characterize the range of input compositions and environmental conditions that succeeds, the conditions that cause failure, and the system's dependence on continuing external inputs. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth and reproducibility within those boundaries; they could not establish literal universality or prove that the same route occurred on early Earth.
completion_criteria.label: Reproduce complete sequence across independent runs and characterize boundaries

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: BIO-01, “Build an autonomously reproducing cell from defined components,” shares the concern with reproduction, but its title centers on constructing a cell. BIO-02 centers on a plausible chemical origin sequence and permits an evolving endpoint that has not reached cellular organization. The supplied roster does not specify which components BIO-01 permits, so it does not support the earlier assertion that BIO-01 allows modern biological components.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-12, “Explain how biological homochirality could emerge and persist,” addresses a potentially relevant chemical constraint: how consistent molecular handedness could arise and remain stable. A proposed BIO-02 route may need to explain its dependence on handed inputs, but explaining homochirality alone would not demonstrate the transition to heritable adaptation. BIO-11, “Reconstruct the major steps in the origin of eukaryotic cells,” concerns a later transition in biological organization and remains a distinct historical and experimental problem.

Roster-based synthesis: BIO-05, “Design functional enzymes to specification across reaction classes,” overlaps through the importance of catalysis. A deliberately designed catalyst could help investigate a reaction while leaving its plausible origin unresolved. BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” could share methods for modeling connected chemical behavior, but a predictive model would not replace the physical demonstration required here. BIO-03, “Predict the effects of genome changes across biological contexts,” shares an interest in consequences of inherited variation while addressing a different predictive capability from the emergence of heredity itself.

change_log.reason: The innovation is coherent and remains distinct from any individual supporting experiment.

change_log.reason: Individual origin-of-life hypotheses are already experimentally testable.

change_log.change: Specified the supplied artificial ribozyme, activated trinucleotide substrates and controlled replenishment in the 2025 experiment.
change_log.reason: These dependencies distinguish the demonstrated replication system from the emergence of replication machinery through a plausible origin sequence.

change_log.change: Integrated fragmentary self-replication, emergent sequence pools and the finite exponential phase followed by plateauing.
change_log.reason: These useful results and limits prevent both understating the experiment and interpreting open-ended replication as unlimited growth or a completed origin transition.

change_log.change: Expanded completion proposals to cover inherited adaptation, controls, disclosed interventions, reproducibility and operating boundaries.
change_log.reason: The endpoint must distinguish sustained adaptation from transient enrichment or drift without presenting proposed tests as established standards.

change_log.change: Replaced the unverified claim about BIO-01's permitted components with a comparison limited to the supplied roster titles.
change_log.reason: The roster supports a comparison of objectives but does not define BIO-01's allowed materials.

change_log.change: Preserved the review's limits concerning underlying experimental materials and later field-wide coverage.
change_log.reason: Full article text supports reporting the dated findings, while absent raw-data inspection and subsequent research leave separate questions unresolved.

unresolved_issues: The supplied record does not establish field-wide completion or continued openness as of November 1, 2026; the dated 2025 result cannot resolve subsequent developments.
Figure images, linked supplementary methods and raw data were not inspected in the supplied review, leaving independent validation of those materials outside this record.
BIO-01's full definition and permitted components remain unavailable; the original claim that it permits modern biological components cannot be retained as established.
The proposed endpoint still needs experiment-specific choices for adaptation duration, environmental challenge, inherited-performance measurements and acceptable intervention dependence.
No supplied evidence identifies a complete plausible route that generates or obtains all necessary replication machinery and substrates while maintaining compatibility through the adaptive endpoint.

brief.title: A chemical path from nonliving matter to evolution
possible: We could watch nonliving chemicals give rise to a population that reproduces, passes on changes and adapts over generations. The experiment would connect the chemical steps under conditions that could plausibly occur in nature, without needing to build a modern cell.
why: Researchers could investigate how chemistry becomes capable of evolution: when inherited information becomes reliable enough for adaptation, and which environmental changes help or disrupt that transition. A complete route would give them a working system for testing these questions.

sources.showed: They repeatedly copied RNA, an information-carrying molecule, by cycling acidity and freezing and thawing. Their system used a supplied RNA catalyst, a molecule that speeds up reactions, and prepared building blocks.
sources.quote: When combined with coupled pH and freeze–thaw cycles, this enabled exponential replication of both (+) and (−) strands of double-stranded RNAs, including a fragment of the ribozyme itself.
sources.cited_for: The work connects separation of paired RNA strands with repeated copying.
sources.not_established: It does not explain how the copying machinery arises from nonliving starting materials or demonstrate sustained inherited adaptation along that route.

sources.who: Stephanie J Zhang, Xiwen Jia, Saurja DasGupta and Jack W Szostak
sources.showed: They chemically energized short RNA pieces and joined them in the same reaction environment, both with and without an RNA catalyst.
sources.quote: Here, we demonstrate that the same chemistry activates oligoribonucleotides and drives both nonenzymatic and ribozyme-catalyzed RNA ligation within the same reaction environment.
sources.cited_for: The work connects preparation of reactive RNA pieces with their assembly.
sources.not_established: It does not connect those reactions to a reproducing population with sustained adaptation.

sources.showed: RNA hosts, which provided copying machinery, evolved alongside parasites that used it. Both diversified and developed defenses and counter-defenses in a system supplied with modern biological machinery.
sources.quote:
The parasitic RNA accumulated unique mutations, thus adding a new
genetic variation to the whole replicator ensemble.
sources.cited_for: The work demonstrates inherited change and adaptation in interacting molecular populations.
sources.not_established: The system depends on supplied biological machinery whose origin from nonliving chemistry it does not explain.

sources.who: Ryo Mizuuchi, Taro Furubayashi and Norikazu Ichihashi
sources.showed: Continuing the RNA evolution experiment produced a network of coexisting hosts and parasites, including cooperation. Additional experiments also produced diversification and relatively stable coexistence.
sources.quote:
The RNA diversi ﬁes into multiple coexisting host and parasite lineages, whose frequencies in
the population initially ﬂuctuate and gradually stabilize.
sources.cited_for: The work demonstrates the emergence of interacting RNA populations and recurring diversification.
sources.not_established: It does not reproduce a complete chemical route from nonliving starting materials to evolution.

shown: Attwater and colleagues connected repeated RNA copying with separation of the copied strands, which otherwise stick together. Zhang and colleagues connected chemical preparation of RNA pieces with their assembly. These experiments resolve particular compatibility problems between stages.

Furubayashi, Mizuuchi and colleagues demonstrated evolving RNA populations that diversified, resisted parasites and formed cooperating networks. Their systems relied on supplied modern biological machinery. The copying experiments also began with an existing catalyst.
missing: A complete route must connect plausible nonliving inputs to a reproducing population that keeps adapting.
The route must account for the formation or natural availability of every essential copying component and building block.
Inherited improvements must persist, rather than reflect temporary enrichment or repeated outside replacement.
The complete sequence must work repeatedly, including in an independent laboratory, with its limits measured.

milestones.label: A connected chemical route produces sustained adaptation
milestones.explanation: A plausible sequence of chemical steps would have to produce a reproducing population that keeps adapting to a changed environment. Compatible conditions and tracked transfers would connect the beginning to the outcome.

milestones.label: Descendants inherit a lasting performance advantage
milestones.explanation: With the challenge and test duration set beforehand, descendants would have to retain an advantage linked to inherited changes. Controlled comparisons would distinguish adaptation from temporary enrichment or outside replacement.

milestones.label: Every essential component and intervention has an account
milestones.explanation: Every functional ingredient and outside intervention would need an identified origin and plausible natural counterpart. An essential component the route cannot make or plausibly obtain would leave the transition incomplete.

milestones.label: The complete route repeats within measured limits
milestones.explanation: The full sequence would have to repeat across independent runs, with reproduction sought in another laboratory and success and failure conditions mapped. This would establish its reliability and dependence on continuing inputs.

uncertain: How long must adaptation persist, and what inherited performance gain would count as convincing?
How much outside replenishment and environmental control can a plausible natural route require?
A successful laboratory route would leave open whether the same sequence occurred on early Earth.

page.title: Prebiotic emergence of Darwinian evolution
page.definition: A connected sequence of reactions converts nonliving starting chemicals available in a specified planetary environment into a reproducing population that inherits variants and evolves by natural selection. The route accounts for the abiotic origin of its replication machinery and substrates.

goal.need: The RNA evolution experiment below supplied an Escherichia coli translation system to make its copying enzyme. RNA strands can reanneal within seconds to minutes, whereas copying takes hours to days. A connected abiotic route would address the origin and chemical compatibility of the machinery needed for heredity and selection.

figures.caption: RNA evolution with supplied translation machinery, published on 18 March 2022
figures.note: One main evolution trajectory; two additional trajectories branched from it. Transfer rounds are laboratory replication–dilution cycles, not measured generations.

completion.title: An abiotic reaction sequence produces a reproducing population that evolves by natural selection.
completion.criterion: A laboratory reaction sequence starts with chemicals and physical conditions supported by a specified geochemical setting and produces a reproducing population. The route accounts for the abiotic formation or availability of every essential catalyst and activated substrate, with chemically compatible transfers and environmental cycles. Descendants inherit molecular variants; variants with higher reproductive success increase under selection during repeated propagation. Essential replication machinery originates within the route instead of being supplied without an abiotic explanation. A modern cell is not required.
completion.set_by: Technology Atlas; no external operational completion test located.
completion.basis: NASA's 2003 and 2008 roadmaps, NSF 16-570, the National Academies' 2019 strategy and origin-of-life prize rules were searched for an end-to-end abiotic-to-evolution assay. None supplied an operational completion threshold for this capability. NASA's requirement to understand a “single integrated system” supports chemical continuity. No numerical generation, fidelity or yield cutoff is added.

milestones.title: A chemical pathway synthesizes prebiotic monomers and condenses them into polymers.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a pathway that synthesizes prebiotic monomers and condenses them into polymers under specified chemical conditions. NASA gives no yield or chain-length cutoff. Zhang et al.'s preprint of 12 July 2025 reports chemical activation and joining of supplied short RNAs in one reaction mixture: about 7% of primer was ligated after 24 h without a ribozyme. This demonstrates an assembly step; the starting oligonucleotides were supplied.
milestones.set_by: NASA, The NASA Astrobiology Roadmap (2008), Objective 3.2; a qualitative programme target.
milestones.threshold_quote: Identify plausible pathways for the synthesis of prebiotic monomers and their condensation into polymers.

milestones.title: Both strands of an RNA duplex are repeatedly copied after product-strand separation.
milestones.criterion: Copy both complementary RNA strands and reuse separated products in further copying cycles. Attwater et al., published on 28 May 2025, coupled pH changes with freeze–thaw cycling and synthesis in ice at −7 °C. Three independent reactions per sampled cycle number showed copying of a ribozyme fragment and its complement. The experiments supplied an evolved RNA catalyst, a ribozyme, and prepared trinucleotide triphosphates, activated three-nucleotide building blocks.
milestones.set_by: The RNA-replication convention stated and experimentally applied by Attwater et al., Nature Chemistry (2025); this criterion concerns RNA.
milestones.threshold_quote: RNA replication comprises the copying of (+) and (−) strands into complementary (−) and (+) daughter strands.

milestones.title: A chemical replication system reproduces its catalysts while substrates are replenished.
milestones.criterion: The system reproduces its replication catalysts while substrates are replenished. Lincoln and Joyce, published on 8 January 2009, demonstrated two cross-catalytic RNA enzymes assembled from four supplied RNA fragments: one serial-transfer experiment used six successive 5 h reactions at 42 °C, transferring 4% each time, and exceeded 10^8-fold amplification per enzyme. Gianni et al., published on 12 February 2026, separately synthesized a 45-nucleotide catalyst and its complement after 72 days at −7 °C, using supplied substrates and a six-nucleotide fragment for catalyst synthesis. Those reactions were not coupled into a propagation cycle.
milestones.set_by: The experimental convention of self-sustained replication defined by Lincoln and Joyce, Science (2009); demonstrated there for cross-catalytic RNA ligases.
milestones.threshold_quote: replication in a self-sustained manner, brought about by enzymatic machinery that is part of the system being replicated.

milestones.title: A chemical population undergoes mutation and natural selection during repeated reproduction.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate inherited variation and differential reproduction in a chemical population under selection. Furubayashi et al., published on 21 July 2020, followed one RNA population for 120 transfers over 600 h; competition assays with three independent replicates showed evolved parasite resistance. Mizuuchi et al., published on 18 March 2022, extended that experiment to a cooperating RNA network. Both studies supplied modern E. coli translation machinery, so they test evolution after that machinery is provided.
milestones.set_by: NASA Astrobiology Roadmap (2003), Objective 3.4; this laboratory target explicitly leaves the historical origin route unrestricted.
milestones.threshold_quote: create and study artificial chemical systems that undergo mutation and natural selection in the laboratory.

not_found: No external completion assay combining abiotic provenance, chemical continuity and heritable adaptation was found in the agency roadmaps, academy strategy or prize rules searched.
NASA's 2015 Astrobiology Strategy PDF exceeded the browser's size limit.
Zhang et al.'s journal full text was blocked at PMC and the publisher; its preprint was accessible.
Replicate counts for Zhang et al.'s 7% ligation time course and Gianni et al.'s self-synthesis assay were not found in the accessible article texts.
No published demonstration of the complete connected abiotic-to-evolution route was found through 14 November 2026.

results.finding: An RNA ribozyme joined supplied trinucleotides into RNA; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The reaction demonstrates polymer assembly, but the trinucleotide substrates and ribozyme were supplied; the source does not demonstrate synthesis of the monomers.
results.quote: The γ fragment synthesis is characterized by multiple sites of initiation and independent ligation of the resulting oligomers, and proceeded effectively, perhaps reflecting the availability of multiple initiation sites.

results.finding: Both strands of a ribozyme fragment were copied across cycles; three independent reactions were sampled per cycle number.
results.detail: Separated products served as templates in a second cycle. The experiment supplied an evolved ribozyme, primers and trinucleotide substrates; polymerization occurred at −7 °C.

results.finding: A ribozyme replicated a fragment of itself; three independent reactions were sampled per cycle number.
results.detail: Fresh reaction mix replenished ribozyme and substrates, but the system copied fragments rather than reproducing a complete active catalyst.
results.quote: These results show that (1) a ribozyme can exponentially replicate part of itself from short building blocks, (2) this ‘fragmentary’ self-replication can occur in a ‘one-pot’ cycled reaction and (3) ribozymes can initiate replication on themselves, even in the absence of a seed template.

results.finding: Short RNA product classes from a random-sequence pool amplified up to 60,000-fold; sample size not stated.
results.detail: Different products accumulated during repeated copying, bearing on differential reproduction. The reported result does not establish inherited mutations and their selection during propagation.

results.finding: One-pot nonenzymatic RNA ligation joined approximately 7% of primer after 24 hours; sample size was not stated.
results.detail: The reaction activated and joined supplied oligonucleotides. It did not demonstrate a pathway synthesizing the monomers and condensing them into polymers.
results.quote: Upon adding an unactivated ligator to the primer–template complex under activation conditions, only ∼7% of the primer was ligated after 24 hours

results.finding: One RNA population encoded a replicase subunit and propagated for 120 transfer rounds with replenishment.
results.detail: The host encoded the catalytic β-subunit, but the active replicase also required EF-Tu and EF-Ts from the supplied E. coli translation system. The complete replication machinery was not reproduced by the system.
results.quote:
The host RNA provides the catalytic
β-subunit of the replicase (via translation), which forms active replicase by
associating with EF-Tu and EF-Ts subunits in the translation system, whereas the
parasitic RNA lacks the intact gene.

results.finding: One RNA population evolved through 120 transfers, with evolved parasite resistance tested in three independent competition assays.
results.detail: Replication errors generated variants, and competition assays showed successive host–parasite adaptations. The experiment supplied a reconstituted E. coli translation system.
results.quote:
During a long-term replication experiment, a clonal population of the
host RNA turned into an evolving host-parasite ecosystem through the continuous
emergence of new types of host and parasitic RNAs produced by replication
errors.

results.finding: RNA-encoded replication catalysts were reproduced in a main experiment and two branched experiments, each reaching 240 rounds.
results.detail: Host RNA encoded a replicase subunit translated by a supplied E. coli system. Each transfer added fresh translation system; the two additional experiments branched from the main population.
results.quote:
The original host RNA replicates via translation of the self-encoded replicase, by
which mutant host RNAs and parasitic RNAs could be generated.

results.finding: In three RNA evolution experiments, host and parasite lineages diversified and coexisted through 240 rounds.
results.detail: The two additional experiments branched from the main experiment and accumulated different mutations. Replication used supplied E. coli translation machinery.
results.quote:
As in the main experiment, we observed similar
gradual diversi ﬁcation and relatively stable coexistence of multi-
ple host and parasitic RNA lineages, despite the accumulation of
different mutations in each additional experiment.

results.finding: Uridine phosphorylation and oligomerization produced oligouridylate up to a tetramer; sample size not reported.
results.detail: DAP and imidazole converted supplied uridine to a nucleotide and oligouridylate under room-temperature paste-reaction conditions.

results.finding: Two cross-replicating RNA enzymes sustained replication through 50 successive transfers.
results.detail: Each transfer supplied fresh substrates; only enzymes carried over from the preceding reaction seeded the next. Reactions ran for 45 minutes at 47 °C.
results.quote: Fifty successive rounds of cross- replication, with transfer of 1% of reacted materials (100-fold dilution) after each round.

results.finding: Five evolved hammerhead RNA variants showed three- to eightfold higher estimated fitness than the starting RNA.
results.detail: Two RNA lineages underwent eight rounds of replication and selection. The higher-fidelity lineage accumulated mutations and enriched fitter variants; reverse transcription, PCR and transcription were used between rounds.
results.quote: The net effect, multiplying the yields from plus- and minus-strand synthesis and the requisite RNA-cleavage activity of the plus strand, is that the evolved variants have an overall three- to eightfold improvement in fitness compared to Seq0

results.finding: Self-replicating chemical population reached steady state after 120 h under flow selection; the experiment was repeated.
results.detail: Seeding experiments showed partial inheritance and frequent mutation. Under flow, the fastest-replicating mutant became most abundant; chemical destruction selected a different distribution. The available structural space and distribution changes were limited.

results.finding: In 2 self-replicating molecular systems, natural selection favored mutants better able to catalyze production of their own replication precursors.
results.detail: Selection depended on the mutants’ ability to activate a photocatalyst that promoted precursor production. The text does not report a quantitative selection effect.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.
